newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-INTER DO MILAN RARE FAVOUR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-INTER DO MILAN RARE FAVOUR.

text.p: Internazionale rarely do neighbours and arch-rivals AC Milan any favours, but their 3-0 humiliation of European champions Juventus in an Italian Cup quarter-final in Turin on Wednesday broke the rule.

Milan are due to meet Juventus in serie A at the same Delle Alpi stadium on Sunday and the first leg cup defeat exposed defensive frailties that Oscar Washington Tabarez's side will be keen to exploit.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi will have his work cut out to restore morale to a defence that will lack three-quarters of his first-choice line-up on Sunday through suspension or injury.
Sergio Porrini, the central defender expected to fill-in for suspended Italy international Ciro Ferrara on Sunday, had a disastrous match against Inter, at fault on two of the goals.
"If that's the real Juventus, then yes I'm worried about Milan," said Lippi, commenting on Juve's worst home defeat in the Italian Cup since a 3-0 set-back against Milan in 1978.
What had looked like a chance for third-place Juventus to open up a five-point serie A lead over the reigning Italian champions suddenly looks like a more evenly balanced encounter.
Milan themselves are struggling for form and consistency under new coach Tabarez and had to come from behind to force a 1-1 draw in their Italian Cup quarter-final with Vicenza on Tuesday.

Now Juventus, after a bright start to the season, have won just three of their last eight matches with their forward line over-reliant on Croat Alen Boksic since the close season departures of Gianluca Vialli and Fabrizio Ravanelli for England's premier league.
Admittedly, the Turin side started the Inter match without Boksic, first-choice goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi and international midfielders Angelo Di Livio and Vladimir Jugovic.

But Italy's Alessandro Del Piero and French international Zinedine Zidane both played in a side that looked a pale shadow of the team that outclassed Inter 2-0 in the league a month ago -- a fact that clearly alarmed Lippi.
"Inter gave us a slap in the face," said Lippi. " There was a huge difference between the two teams in concentration and character.
"Perhaps it's the praise and prizes that we have won," he added "We've lost our humility."
If Juventus are getting too big for their boots, Milan are having problems filling their own.
Coach Tabarez looks certain to start the match without injured Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic and there are doubts over defender Marcel Desailly.
The French international pulled a calf muscle in Milan's draw with Vicenza on Tuesday.
There are also continuing question marks over the much anticipated return of Franco Baresi at the heart of Milan's porous defence - currently conceding a goal a game without him.
The 36-year-old captain, in his last season with Milan, has seen just 90 minutes of league action thanks to a niggling knee injury.
Paolo Maldini (groin strain) and Alessandro Costacurta (knee) are also carrying injuries but should start the match.
With Christian Panucci suspended for one game, Tabarez is likely to prefer Costacurta to Dutch international Michael Reiziger at right back.
The presence of Roberto Baggio on his old hunting ground is still up in the air.
The former Juventus striker, back in form after 12 injury-filled months, is unlikely to win his front-line place back from Marco Simone but could start in midfield.
"I understand that it's an embarrassing situation (for Tabarez)," the former European footballer of the year told Gazzetta dello Sport on Thursday. "But I feel in form and ready."
